title: The Possession of Father and Son
english: Having said to him, 'I am your God', he who is outside the right faith and the keeping of Christ's commandments is an atheist, having excluded himself from having God; and since he is an atheist by having led himself away from divine instruction in the said manner, he who remains in it has a father and a son. For in the one keeping his word, the Son said he would come together with the Father upon the remaining, having been built as a holy temple from the keeping of the divine commandments. And since having God is twofold, the one part being common to all creatures, signifying the same as having a Creator, and the other part remaining for only those healing him through moral excellence, as it is signified: 'God is to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob' (Exodus 6:3) and altogether to the Hebrews. Believe also those things which shall be said thus: 'he who has the Son', he says, 'also has the Father' and again, as to be persuaded of the divinity of the consubstantiality from this: since the Father is in the Son, he who has the Son has also the Father; but again and conversely: he who has the Father has also the Son existing in the Father.

If anyone wishes to object, saying: 'and he who has disciples has the Son, and he who has the Son has the Father' according to: 'he who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me' (Matthew 10:40), it is not the way to object; for these things are said concerning instruction. Since he who received the apostles agreed with their instruction, he received through them a Father and Son teaching; and differently: since also he who remains in the teaching has the Father and the Son, and the apostles remained in the teaching as also to preach it, he who received them being a temple of God through him who receives them, has the Son and Father in them.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
